title: Primes in arithmetic progressions with power-saving error from zero-free half-planes of Dirichlet L-functions
abstract: For a fixed modulus q and a residue a coprime to q: if ζ(s) and every L(s, χ) with χ a nontrivial Dirichlet character mod q have no zeros with real part greater than θ (1/2 ≤ θ < 1), then ψ(x; q, a) = x/φ(q) + O(x^{θ+δ}) for every δ > 0. Consequently the zero-free half-plane Re s > 7/8 for all Dirichlet L-functions (proved by OpenAI in 2026, used here as an explicitly stated hypothesis, verbatim) yields the prime number theorem in arithmetic progressions with error O(x^{7/8+δ}). Proof: for each χ ≠ 1, a smoothed twisted Chebyshev function, a contour shift (no residue, L entire), a bound L'/L(σ+it, χ) ≪ log|t| via Borel–Carathéodory after continuing L to Re s > 0 with a polynomial growth bound, then orthogonality of characters and the ζ case for the trivial character.
